items.author: Ben (2026-09-25, the round-feedback form after the sprint-47 live clicks); filed by Claude
items.title: Roads are a tree plus a detour test, and only villages above a size spur: no lattice, and round 6's tail inside 35 s
items.design:
MOVED (2026-10-07, the sprint 49 close-out; Ben: place by subject): sprint 49 -> 50. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-25, the density form): the village spur floor is 40,000 heads (the ladder's ~p90; median road pass 18 s loaded, 1 of 16 seeds under 10 s), size read as the population step's headcount; a border link ends ONLY on a town or a spurring village (LOGISTICS.md § 4). The street carpet is not this item's: BL-1130 (centres consolidate) thins the centres upstream, and this item's "no lattice on the densest seed" is read after it.

ROUND 2 (the lane's own findings and the settle review): fix the floor at 40,000 as the constant; border endpoints restricted to towns and spurring villages; road_generation.cpp's two hand-written cache clears (~616-619, ~689-691) replaced by invalidate_logistics_caches so the new nearest-anchor field is never missed; the loading bar's roads weight (hard_coded_world.cpp ~495, 38,000 ms) and kBorderUnitsPerNation re-measured; road_generation_harness's "R2 highway tier reachable when qualified" FAILS on 0 of 8 seeds, identically on b03fd52e -- find why (the percentile gate, the two-major-endpoints rule, or the harness's qualified regen) and fix the cause or split it to its own item with the reading; never weaken the row.

SPRINT 48 CUT (Ben, 2026-09-25, the cut form): BL-1077 (village roads cost) is FOLDED IN. Its target joins this done-when: generate_roads under ~10 s Release on the library seeds, read after the spur floor; if the floor alone does not reach it, BL-1077's bound (one multi-source search per centre, or a shared reach field, digest-neutral by itself) is this item's second step. THE 35 s IS JUDGED ON THE WHOLE TAIL, jointly with BL-1117 (settle tick one), which joins the sprint with its fix: on seed 0 the settle is ~56 s Release, tick 1 alone 38.5 s, so roads alone cannot meet it.

FILED 2026-09-25 (Ben, walking round 6: "we also need many fewer roads... it should be heavily discouraged to build a lattice of roads"; he chose the tree plus a detour test over "no second path", and spurs only for villages above a size). LOGISTICS.md § 4 carries the rule; STARTUP.md § Round 6 carries the 35 s target.

THE WORK. (1) Replace the relative-neighbour redundancy edges with the DETOUR TEST: after the Kruskal MST, a candidate link between two centres is laid only when the network's route between them costs more than 2x the direct A* route (one constant, named). The percentile rationing of loops applies to the loops the test admits (a delegated reading that keeps BL-618/BL-621 intact; Ben may overturn). (2) A village lays a spur only above a size floor, MEASURED on the 16 curated seeds first (Rule 0b: road tiles, spur count and pass time per floor candidate). (3) The border link rule is unchanged.

A WORLD-MOVER: every road digest and the sweep pins move -- read road tile counts, pass time (gen_step_costs --finish) and the haulage baseline (memory: goldens cannot see trade) on the 16 seeds before and after, then ONE re-bless.

DONE WHEN. No lattice on a capture of the densest seed; road pass time and tile count recorded old -> new per seed; round 6's tail lands within 35 s of arrival on seeds 0 and 28 in Release (gen_step_costs); one re-bless; road_generation_harness green (connectivity held). CARRIED to sprint 49 at the sprint 48 close (2026-10-04): owed R4 a quiet Release gen_step_costs run on 16 seeds (road tiles and pass time per seed, old -> new, against ~10 s); R6 an isolated haulage reading of this change (or fold into BL-1165); R7 a cold review of round 4 (8b921ee6, directed paths).

items.title: Trace the three movements the sprint 48 re-bless could not attribute: population halved, haulage fell, nation units fell
items.design:

Ben authorised the sprint 48 re-bless (2026-10-03, merged 179615b8) with three untraced movements filed here: (1) world population 12.19B -> 6.27B (likeliest BL-1130/1132, the doubled war); (2) shipped haulage (--far-trade) 16,327 / 14,729 -> 14,434 / 11,917 per year (-11.6% / -19.1%), rising on 8 seeds and falling on 8, though every item that read it alone reported a rise or no change (likeliest BL-1125's folds); (3) nation units 414,404 -> 167,110. WORK: bisect each across the sprint's merge commits with rebless_shape_probe (v0.1.26 e50ab81c -> a899bb2a), name the cause, and report for Ben whether each is wanted. Also untraced there: road tiers flipping whole national networks Road/Highway on seeds 28, 31, 37 (Highway gate percentile tie, inferred); BL-1168's -35.6% haulage (a third fewer corporations, inferred). See docs/development/drafts/sprint-48-rebless-2.md.

items.author: Claude (BL-1172 cold review, 2026-10-03)
items.title: The construction panels predict the build rate the tick will actually take
items.design: MOVED (2026-10-07, the sprint 49 close-out; Ben: place by subject): sprint 49 -> 51. construction_panel.cpp:60 and selection_panel.cpp:267 predict a site's rate from m->supply[r]. The tick draws from shelf inventory gated by the fair-price ceiling (shelf_admits, components.hpp), pauses a build on a material posted over the ceiling, and stretches it on capacity over the ceiling (FINANCE.md, Ben 2026-10-03). The panels already missed the inventory read and the stretch rule; the ceiling widens the gap, so a paused build can show progress. Read the tick's own expression rather than a second copy. Needs a live click to verify.

items.author: Claude (the BL-1186 routing lane, 2026-10-04)
items.title: A convoy is drawn, seen and interdicted along the legs it actually travels
items.design:
MOVED (2026-10-07, the sprint 49 close-out; Ben: place by subject): sprint 49 -> 50. PULLED INTO SPRINT 49 (2026-10-04, the BL-1186 cold review): not only drawing - position, vision and interdiction read the unconfined centre-to-centre path, so a land-fallback convoy is interdicted on water it never enters and immune on the land it crosses, a capture credits the pool of a water tile, and a hostile unit on a sea route's inland leg never intercepts. A gameplay error until fixed.

After BL-1186 routes water crossings as land -> port -> sea -> port -> land, convoy_route_tiles still lays the lane as the direct centre-to-centre path, so the vision beam, the convoy's drawn position and interdiction all read a route the cargo does not take. Make convoy_route_tiles return the leg route.

items.author: Claude (the BL-1206 lane, 2026-10-07)
items.title: A specialist's own-fed recipe is not always refined fuel
items.design: Found by BL-1206 (seat day-1 profit, 2026-10-07). 13 of 16 seat kits open on refined_fuel: generation picks the FIRST own-fed recipe in browse order and petroleum is co-extracted widely, so most specialists make refined fuel, it gluts by tick 4, and the loss reflex fires. Break the tie by what the kit's market is short of (derived demand), not browse order.

items.design: Found by BL-1206 (seat day-1 profit, 2026-10-07). Seed 0: a trade-focus kit places its processor in a different market from its only extraction site, so no recipe it could take is own-fed, and its steel starves on a thin coal shelf. A seat kit's processor should stand where its own extraction delivers.

items.author: Claude (the sprint 49 close-out; Ben, the close-out form, 2026-10-07)
items.title: A built processor gets its inputs, so 70% are running at handoff
items.design: CARRIED from sprint 49 (Ben, the close-out form, 2026-10-07: close with G1 unmet, carry it to sprint 50 as a logistics item). The 16-seed market_viability reading on main after BL-1183 C1: G1 54.7% of built processors running at handoff against Ben's 70% (G2 54.4 and G3 88.9 pass). About a quarter of built processors are already decommissioned by the handoff, and by their last reported state almost all were input-starved (half A: 578 of 674). Diagnose which inputs fail to arrive, at which markets, and why - no producer within reach, a producer whose surplus is not dispatched, or a dispatch the margin refuses - then fix the cause in the network or dispatch, not by clamping the loss reflex. Re-measure construction stalls here too: whether a stalled site is ever abandoned (BL-1183 C3) is still unruled. Judge it on the market-viability skill, 16 seeds.

items.author: Ben (the direction, 2026-10-08); Claude (the open calls)
items.title: The player is a nation with a space programme, not a corporation holding a seat
items.design: Ben, 2026-10-08: the player becomes a NATION with a space programme (option A, chosen over B - a state-chartered space corporation under an AI-run parent). Reason, in his words: "there are many more gameplay systems available to a nation, and there's no real advantage to being just a corporation." Shape as he put it: the player starts with a space corporation tied directly to its parent nation; acquisitions and funding still work internationally. A generation parameter tunes HOW MANY nations run a space programme, and the seat shortlist draws from those. This reverses NR-885 (corporation holding a seat, 2026-09-17). OPEN CALLS before the doc sweep (NR-980): (1) which nation verbs the player holds - budget weights, tariffs, law, territory, force production - and whether any stay closed; (2) the nation step and the grant register (AI_OPPONENT.md § 11) must stop acting on the player's own nation - a narrowing, recorded as such; (3) the FIELD / ANSWER-TO design test assumes a power above the player - what replaces 'answer to' for a state (rivals, its own population, the Era 1 nuclear test); (4) the space corporation: a separate actor the player directs (keeping the corp systems, acquisitions, international funding) or folded into the nation's space_programme line - and the 'player's corp is never a supplier to a state purchase' rule inverts for the player's own nation; (5) the generation parameter: how many nations run a space programme, its default, and what a non-programme nation does; (6) elimination: CONCEPT's 'parent nation must also be destroyed' becomes the whole rule. SWEEP once ruled: CONCEPT § Player identity, STARTUP § The seat, NATIONS (space_programme supplier rule; law subject vs legislator), MANUAL § 1.2, SYSTEMS § Policy, AI_OPPONENT § 11, standing rules' 'player's own corp' wording, and every doc NR-885's sweep touched (09a1b567).
